summary: All 6 phases complete. Closed the extension loader's symlink data-loss bug: remove_installed_files() now skips (never deletes) any file-level symlink or any file reached through a symlinked ancestor directory, bounded by opts.project_dir, returning a new skipped_count. Made .syncprotect protection symmetric between copy and remove by filtering at the init.lua call sites (manager.unload never called load_syncprotect before this fix). Made the copy path (copy_simple_files, copy_skill_dirs) symlink-preserving so symlink deploy mode survives a full unload/load cycle without flattening. Proved the fix empirically at every layer: a scratch unit test proves Case A (ancestor-symlinked file) source destroyed pre-fix and survives post-fix; a scratch .syncprotect test confirms key-shape symmetry with copy_file; a scratch copy-path test confirms symlinks survive copy operations; and a full scratch integration test exercises the REAL manager.load/unload/reload functions end-to-end, proving zero data loss and zero flattening for symlink deploy mode while ordinary copy deploy mode still works. Restored the two previously-flattened symlinks (.claude/agents/literature-agent.md, .claude/commands/literature.md) after verifying byte-identical content, and recorded the ownership rule durably in a new context document. No loader operation was ever run against the real .claude/ tree; all destructive testing occurred under the scratchpad only.

artifacts.summary: Full implementation summary covering all 6 phases: what changed, key decisions, plan deviations (3 methodology substitutions, no scope changes), verification evidence per phase, and two notes -- a shared-session side effect in the index.json commit diff, and the deferred dangling zotero symlink cleanup.

next_action_hint: Implementation complete and verified. Consider the possible follow-ups recorded in the plan's Non-Goals: (1) dangling skill-zotero/zotero.md symlink cleanup, provably inert but unrelated housekeeping; (2) an installed_symlinks state category (research Finding 5's optional refactor) if per-extension deploy-mode tracking becomes valuable later; (3) an install-extension.sh-style target-mismatch warning on the copy path, closed as a side effect by the ownership rule but not explicitly guarded. None of these are required for this fix to be complete and safe.
decisions_made: Followed the plan's design exactly: skip-and-warn on the remove side rather than unlink-the-ancestor, because loader.lua cannot recreate symlinks it destroys and manager.reload's unload-then-load sequencing means unlinking on remove would destroy the pre-existing-symlink signal the copy-side guard depends on.

Phase 2 discriminating-power proof substituted loadfile()-based shadow-module override for the plan's suggested git-stash approach, because Neovim's runtimepath-based require() loader ignores package.path ordering for files under ~/.config/nvim even under -u NONE. Verified via debug.getinfo() that the override correctly resolved to the pre-fix shadow file. This never touched the real tracked loader.lua.

Phase 5 integration test substituted load-then-convert-to-symlink for the plan's hand-author-extensions.json suggestion, more faithfully reproducing the actual incident sequence (an extension loaded once via copy, later converted to symlink deploy mode by install-extension.sh independently, leaving extensions.json state unaware of the conversion).

Phase 6 restored the two flattened symlinks via rm + ln -s rather than git checkout HEAD -- <path>, per explicit orchestrator direction: git checkout -- <path> is blocked by this repo's guard-destructive-git.sh PreToolUse hook without a full-tree git stash snapshot first, which was avoided given other tasks' concurrent uncommitted work in this shared session.
Verified before restoring: both flattened files were byte-identical to their extension source (diffed against the target resolved from git HEAD's recorded symlink blob content, not assumed).
dead_ends: Attempted git checkout HEAD -- <path> for Phase 6 symlink restoration first; blocked by guard-destructive-git.sh's uncommitted-changes protection. Switched to rm + ln -s per orchestrator direction, achieving an identical result without the snapshot requirement.
